metadata.based_on: CIS Ubuntu Linux 22.04 LTS Benchmark v1.0.0

controls.title: Ensure permissions on /etc/ssh/sshd_config are configured
controls.justification: Prevents unauthorized modification of SSH daemon configuration. If sshd_config is world-readable, an attacker with low privileges can enumerate allowed users, authentication methods, and other SSH parameters to plan lateral movement.

controls.title: Ensure SSH Protocol is set to 2
controls.justification: SSH Protocol 1 has known vulnerabilities including man-in-the-middle attacks and session injection. Protocol 2 is the secure standard. All MedDefense servers must enforce Protocol 2 exclusively.

controls.title: Ensure SSH X11 forwarding is disabled
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 4 (lateral movement via X11 tunneling)
controls.justification: X11 forwarding allows graphical application tunneling over SSH, which can be abused by attackers to exfiltrate data or establish backdoor graphical sessions. Clinical servers have no legitimate need for X11 forwarding.

controls.title: Ensure SSH MaxAuthTries is set to 4 or less
controls.threat_mapping: 1x02-F009, Crimson Tide Phase 2 (credential brute force via SSH)
controls.justification: Limiting authentication attempts reduces the risk of brute-force password attacks against SSH. Combined with password authentication disabled (CIS-5.2.8), this provides defense in depth against credential guessing.

controls.title: Ensure SSH root login is disabled
controls.threat_mapping: 1x02-F009, Crimson Tide Phase 3 (privilege escalation via root SSH)
controls.justification: Direct root login over SSH bypasses accountability (no audit trail of which admin escalated). All administrative access must use named accounts with sudo, ensuring audit logs capture the identity of every privileged action.

controls.title: Ensure SSH password authentication is disabled
controls.threat_mapping: 1x02-F009, Crimson Tide Phase 3 (SSH lateral movement with stolen credentials)
controls.justification: Password authentication over SSH is the primary lateral movement vector for ransomware actors. Crimson Tide specifically uses SSH with credentials cracked via Kerberoasting. Key-only authentication eliminates this vector because private keys cannot be cracked offline.

controls.title: Ensure SSH Idle Timeout Interval is configured
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 4 (persistent SSH sessions for lateral movement)
controls.justification: Idle SSH sessions are a security risk—an attacker can maintain persistence by keeping a session open indefinitely. A 5-minute idle timeout (300 seconds) with zero keepalive attempts automatically terminates abandoned sessions.

controls.title: Ensure IPv4 forwarding is disabled
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 4 (lateral movement via compromised server as pivot)
controls.justification: IP forwarding allows a compromised server to route traffic between networks, becoming a pivot point for lateral movement. MedDefense servers are endpoints, not routers—this capability must be explicitly disabled.

controls.title: Ensure packet redirect sending is disabled
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 5 (traffic redirection for MITM interception)
controls.justification: ICMP redirects can be abused by an on-path attacker to redirect traffic and perform man-in-the-middle interception. MedDefense's flat network makes this attack feasible. Disabling redirects closes this vector.

controls.title: Ensure source routed packets are not accepted
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 4 (source-routed lateral movement to bypass network ACLs)
controls.justification: Source-routed packets allow the sender to specify the network path, potentially bypassing firewall rules and network ACLs. This must be disabled on all MedDefense servers to prevent route manipulation attacks.

controls.title: Ensure TCP SYN Cookies is enabled
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 7 (DoS during ransomware encryption to delay response)
controls.justification: SYN flood attacks can overwhelm a server's connection table, causing denial of service. SYN cookies cryptographically validate connection requests without consuming server resources until the handshake completes, mitigating SYN flood DoS attacks.

controls.title: Ensure AppArmor is installed and enforcing
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 5 (defense evasion via unrestricted process execution)
controls.implementation_task: apt-get install -y apparmor apparmor-profiles apparmor-utils && aa-enforce /etc/apparmor.d/*
controls.verification_method: aa-status | grep 'profiles are loaded' && aa-status | grep 'enforce mode'
controls.justification: AppArmor (integrated by default in Ubuntu per AppArmor Wiki) confines services to their required filesystem paths and capabilities. If an attacker compromises Apache on web-srv-01, AppArmor prevents the process from reading /etc/shadow or executing a reverse shell binary. This is mandatory access control—defense in depth at the kernel level.

controls.title: Ensure auditd is installed and enabled
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 5 (log clearing to erase forensic evidence)
controls.implementation_task: apt-get install -y auditd audispd-plugins && systemctl enable auditd && systemctl start auditd
controls.justification: auditd provides kernel-level logging of security-relevant events: file access, privilege escalation, command execution. Crimson Tide specifically clears Windows Event Logs; Linux auditd logs forwarded to log-srv-01 survive local clearing. Without auditd, MedDefense has no forensic trail of an attacker's actions.

controls.title: Ensure host-based firewall (UFW) is installed and active
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 4 (unrestricted lateral movement on flat network)
controls.implementation_task: apt-get install -y ufw && ufw default deny incoming && ufw allow from 10.10.10.0/24 to any port 22 proto tcp && ufw enable
controls.justification: MedDefense operates on a flat network with no internal segmentation. A host-based firewall with default-deny posture provides the last line of defense against lateral movement. Even if network segmentation is not yet deployed, UFW on each server restricts which systems can connect to SSH, MySQL, and other services.

controls.title: Ensure permissions on /etc/crontab are configured
controls.threat_mapping: Crimson Tide Phase 2 (persistence via malicious cron jobs)
controls.justification: Cron jobs execute with the privileges of their owner. World-readable crontab files expose scheduled tasks, including backup scripts that may contain credentials. Restrictive permissions prevent enumeration and unauthorized modification of scheduled tasks.
